descriptions: the Lord (pati) as the one independent cause, acting by his own will
the Lord's knowledge and action are unsurpassed; liberation brings the soul into his proximity and union, sharing his powers (Pāśupata)
for the skull-observers the Lord is Kapālin/Bhairava, whose penance they re-enact
negations: the Lord is not dependent on karma (PABh on PS 2.6)
relation_to_self: Souls are eternal paśus distinct from the Lord; liberation is the end of their suffering by the Lord's grace.
relation_to_world: The Lord emits and withdraws the effects (the world and the embodied souls) at will; he is their cause.
caveat: The Atimārga schools are theistic and keep the liberated soul distinct from the Lord; they would reject a reading that dissolves the soul into an impersonal absolute. The Mantramārga ranks their goal below its own (Svacchanda 11.71). For the Lākula, Kāpālika and Kālāmukha divisions almost no first-hand doctrinal text survives.

descriptions: Pati: he 'reaches' and 'protects' the paśus by an infinite power of knowledge and by his lordship (PABh on PS 1.1).
Kāraṇa: by will (kāmitva) he produces the whole effect - vidyā, kalā and paśu - all at once or in sequence as he wishes (PABh on PS 2.5-6).
His activity is play (krīḍā): he produces, favours and conceals the threefold effect (PABh on PS 1.9).
Īśāna of all knowledges, lord of all beings, overlord of Brahman, Brahmā; 'may Śiva be mine, always Śiva' (PS 5.42-47, the Īśāna mantra).
Śaṅkara, maker of all happiness and nirvāṇa (PABh on PS 2.20).
negations: he does not depend on karma or on the soul (na karmāpekṣa, PABh on PS 2.6)
he alone is not a paśu (PABh on PS 1.1)
relation_to_self: The paśus are all sentient beings other than the Lord, even the gods from Brahmā down and those liberated by Sāṃkhya-Yoga; their bondage is lack of lordship (anaiśvarya). By the rule of practice and the Lord's grace the soul reaches Rudra's proximity (PS 4.19) and union (sāyujya, PS 5.33) and gains his powers of knowing and acting; the Lord alone remains the independent cause.
relation_to_world: The effect - the insentient kalās (elements, qualities, organs) and the souls - is eternal yet wholly dependent on the Lord's will; he emits, maintains, withdraws and favours it.
caveat: Pāśupata theism keeps the Lord and the soul distinct even in liberation and makes the Lord only the (efficient) cause; it would reject both an impersonal absolute in which the soul dissolves and the Vedāntin claim (BS 2.2.37) that the Lord must also be the material cause.

descriptions: The Svacchanda Tantra says the skull-observers and the Pāśupatas stand 'in the Īśvara and in the Dhruva' and are not re-created (11.184); the Lākula goal is thus described by others as a fixed level beyond rebirth.
relation_to_self: Not recorded in the tradition's own words.
relation_to_world: Not recorded in the tradition's own words; scholarship reports an expanded hierarchy of worlds.
caveat: Reconstructed entirely from others' texts; any statement of the Lākula view of the ultimate is provisional.

names.name: Soma (Śiva 'with Umā'; name of the doctrine Somasiddhānta)

descriptions: Worshipped as Mahābhairava (Prabodhacandrodaya act 3, an opponent's portrayal).
Kapālin: the skull-bearing form of Śiva whose penance for Brahmā's head the Kāpālika imitates (Kūrma P. 2.31).
relation_to_self: Yāmuna reports that for the Kāpālikas liberation comes from knowing and wearing the six insignia and from a meditation on the self, not from knowledge of Brahman (opponent's report).
relation_to_world: Not recorded in the tradition's own words.
caveat: Known almost entirely through opponents and satirists; no Kāpālika scripture has been identified with certainty. Somasiddhānta, the name of their doctrine, is attested; its content is not.

descriptions: Inscriptions praise Kālāmukha ācāryas as devotees of Śiva and masters of the Lakula-siddhānta; no Kālāmukha doctrinal treatise survives.
relation_to_self: Not recorded in the tradition's own words.
relation_to_world: Not recorded in the tradition's own words.
caveat: Known only from inscriptions and from opponents (Yāmuna, Rāmānuja).
